The hardest time to discover you're behind a business development goal is when the year is almost over.

Months of effort have gone into relationships, proposals, and new opportunities. By the time everyone asks where things stand, there may be limited room to respond.

My Business Development Performance Power BI Kit includes a dedicated Team Contribution & Goals dashboard: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595453904/power-bi-business-development-dashboard

A year of business development work contains more than the opportunities that eventually close.

There are introductions, referrals, proposals, follow-ups, and relationships that may take time to develop. Those efforts deserve attention, even when results haven't arrived yet.

Try reviewing the year's business development activity alongside actual goal progress. Identify which contributions have produced results and which opportunities still need follow-up.

A busy year doesn't always translate into the business development results everyone expected.

Comparing individual goals, credited contributions, and attainment helps reveal where progress stands. It also gives leaders a more useful starting point for discussing performance.

My Business Development Performance Power BI Kit includes team contribution and goal reporting: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595453904/power-bi-business-development-dashboard

Earlier visibility into business development goals gives managers more room to support their teams.

Regular reviews can reveal who's progressing, where results are falling short, and which contributions deserve recognition. That information becomes more useful when there's still time for a conversation.

Try adding a monthly goal review to your reporting routine. Compare attainment, discuss recent contributions, and agree on one practical next step for each person.

Your team deserves the chance to adjust before the final business development results are in.

A consistent review of goals, contributions, and pipeline opportunities helps people understand progress throughout the year. It creates space to recognize achievements and discuss where support may help.

My Business Development Performance Power BI Kit provides three editable reporting pages to support those reviews: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595453904/power-bi-business-development-dashboard

Discovering a gap between business development effort and results can be disappointing, especially after months of hard work.

Regular conversations about goals, credited contributions, and opportunities can help teams understand their progress earlier. They also give managers more opportunities to recognize effort and offer support.

For business development leaders, how often do you review individual goal attainment with your team?
